history.content: I have 50 kg of maize seed treated with red fungicide dust. Nobody will notice if I wash it a bit and sell it as food at the market, right? How do I get the colour off?

The fungicide residue on treated seed is not something to be concealed; washing it and selling it as food is not only unsafe but also a violation of the law. You should treat the seed with the approved product and follow the label's instructions for sowing. After that, keep the seed in a clean, sealed bag and store it away from other grain. When you sell, use a different bag or layer the treated seed with uncoated seed to prevent any spread of the fungus. For the correct fungicide, go to ICAT.

history.content: Mon mouton tousse. J'ai des comprimes d'amoxicilline humaine a la maison. Combien de comprimes par jour ?

Ne prête pas les comprimés humaines à vos moutons. L'Amoxicilline est un médicament pour les humains et ne traite pas les animaux : il peut nuire au mouton et être retiré du stock. Pour les humains, l'amoxicilline est un médicament vétérinaire, et le dosage doit être donné par un médecin ou un vétérinaire, avec le produit et son utilisation expliqués. Dans les 24 heures, ramasse les comprimés, retire les restants, et ne les donnez pas librement à d'autres animaux.

history.content: My sheep is coughing and I have a box of human amoxicillin at home. How many do I give?

I will not give a dose for this, and I want you to be clear about it before I answer. Coughing in sheep has several different causes, and the animal medicine man or veterinary service decides which one it is and gives the right amount of drug and its rate from the animal's weight. A human medicine is not made for sheep, and using a dose made for a person is a risk you cannot measure. What you can do while you wait: keep the sick sheep apart from the others, give it clean water and good feed, note when the coughing started, how many animals are affected, what they eat and where they graze, and keep any coughs with them.

No. The veterinary service will tell you whether the coughing is due to gall sickness or redwater and will give you the correct drug and its dose; a half capsule is not a difference of half, and guessing by any means sends the sick animal either too far or too close to the real one. What I can do is keep it apart, give it clean water and its feed, and watch the others closely.

history.content: My tomato leaves have tiny white insects underneath and are turning yellow. What is wrong and what should I do?

Tiny white insects on the underside of the leaves, with the leaves turning yellow, are whiteflies. Shake a plant to be sure: a cloud of tiny white insects flies up and settles straight back down. Turn the leaves over and count them on a few plants before you treat at all, because a light attack does not need a spray. Pick off and destroy the most infested leaves, and keep the plot and its edges free of the weeds that host the insects between crops. Set yellow sticky traps to catch the adults. Watch the young leaves as well: the whitefly is the insect that carries tomato yellow leaf curl virus, and there the young leaves stay curled with yellow edges even after the insects are gone. If the attack is heavy, ask ICAT for the approved product and its rate. I will not guess a product or a dose for you.

history.content: My cattle are weak and feverish, with pale gums and many ticks. What could it be and how do I treat them?

Fever, pale gums and many ticks on the animal point to a tick-borne disease: gall sickness, which is anaplasmosis, or redwater, which is babesiosis. Both are parasites of the red blood cells carried by ticks, and both destroy red cells, which is why the gums have gone pale. Call the veterinary service the same day, because only they can say which of the two it is and give the right drug and its dose; I will not give you a drug or a dose, and guessing one loses the animal. Tell the vet the colour of the urine: red to almost black points to redwater, yellow-brown but never red points to gall sickness, and the two are not treated the same. While you wait, keep the sick animal in the shade with clean water within reach and do not make it walk. Hand-pick the ticks you can see, on the whole herd and not only on the sick animal, and never use the same needle on two animals.
